title: The integral dualizing object and its adjunction
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], so $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ has characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$. Put $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $a:X\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the structure morphism of a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, and let $d\ge0$ with $\dim X\le d$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. On $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ write $R_X=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_X$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and use ordinary sheaves of modules over these ring sheaves, not a different continuous or condensed coefficient category. Let $Ra_n^!$ be the finite constructible comparison-class exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and put $\omega_{X,n}=Ra_n^!(A_n)_s$.

There is a derived-complete object [def-weil-derived-complete]
$$\omega_{X,R}=R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_n\omega_{X,n},\qquad\omega_{X,R}\otimes^L_{R_X}(A_n)_X\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{X,n}.$$
Here $\operatorname{Res}_n$ is restriction of scalars along $R_X\to(A_n)_X$, the finite transitions are adjoint to the counit-defined coefficient comparisons, and $R\lim$ is the total right derived inverse limit of a strict realization of that tower [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. The object belongs to $D^b_c(X,R)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and every reduction has Tor amplitude in $[-2d,0]$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].

For every $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ there is a natural isomorphism in $D(R)$
$$\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,\omega_{X,R})\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,R),\qquad C=\Gamma(s,Ra_!K).$$
Here $Ra_!$ is integral compact support [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], sections at $s$ are the coefficient-point functor [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], and $\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,L)=R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{proet}},R\mathcal Hom_{R_X}(K,L))$ is the global derived mapping complex [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Thus $\omega_{X,R}$ represents the right-adjoint value at $R_s$: taking $H^0$ gives $\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,\omega_{X,R})\cong\operatorname{Hom}_s(Ra_!K,R_s)$. This is the value-at-the-coefficient-unit assertion; it does not use existence of an integral exceptional adjoint on arbitrary target inputs.

proof.text: Construct a strict normalized finite-dualizing tower T, its isomorphisms e_n and its published-limit Roos triangle using lem-coef-integral-dualizing-roos-model. Set M equal to the value of integralDualizingLimit on T.

Apply normalizedDVRTower_effectivity to the supplied Roos maps. It gives invertible canonical reduction counits, their coherence for every quotient, and legacy derived completeness. The existing sfDerivedComplete_iff_legacy transports completeness to IsSfDerivedComplete.

For each n compose the counit isomorphism M tensor^L A_n ≅ T.M_n with e_n. Apply lem-coef-integral-dualizing-finite-bounds. These give the single support interval [-2d,0] for every constructible reduction, proving sfIntegralConstructible M, and the asserted uniform reduction Tor interval.

Bundle M with this membership proof, and apply lem-coef-integral-dualizing-mapping-limit with the same T, e and coherent presentation. Return the pointwise isomorphisms e_n, their given transition equation, the identity comparison of M to the published limit, the presentation, the Tor bounds and both mapping adjunctions.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $R=\mathcal O_E$ and $A_n=A_{E,n}$. Write $a:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$,
$\dim X\leq d$, $\omega_{X,n}=Ra_n^!A_n$, and

$$
\omega_{X,R}=Ra^!_R R\in D^b_c(X,R),
$$

the value at $R$ of the right adjoint of $Ra_!$ on $D^b_c(-,R)$
([sk-thm-existence], [sk-prop-sf-existence]). Then

$$
\omega_{X,R}\otimes_R^L A_n\cong\omega_{X,n},
\qquad
\omega_{X,R}\cong R\varprojlim_n\omega_{X,n},
$$

and $\omega_{X,R}$ has uniform reduction Tor interval $[-2d,0]$. For
$K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ there is a natural isomorphism of derived mapping complexes

$$
R\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,\omega_{X,R})
\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_R(Ra_!K,R).
$$

proof.text:
By [sk-thm-existence], (3) and (4), $Ra^!_R$ exists and sends
$D^b_c(\operatorname{Spec}k,R)$ into $D^b_c(X,R)$, so $\omega_{X,R}\in D^b_c(X,R)$.
The coefficient comparison for the exceptional inverse image along
$R\to A_n$ is an isomorphism $\omega_{X,R}\otimes^{\mathbf L}_RA_n\cong\omega_{X,n}$
([sk-prop-scalar-six]), compatible with the reductions $A_n\to A_m$ and with the
comparisons of [lem-coef-finite-dualizing]. Objects of $D^b_c(X,R)$ are
derived complete ([def-pe-derived-complete], [sk-prop-integral-criterion]), so
$\omega_{X,R}\cong R\varprojlim_n\omega_{X,R}\otimes^{\mathbf L}_RA_n
\cong R\varprojlim_n\omega_{X,n}$. The Tor interval is read off on the
reductions. The finite preservation bound of
[lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata], transported by
[lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison], gives $[-2d,0]$ for $\omega_{X,n}$,
by taking the constant input.

For the adjunction, the map

$$
R\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,\omega_{X,R})\xrightarrow{Ra_!}
R\operatorname{Hom}(Ra_!K,Ra_!\omega_{X,R})\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}
R\operatorname{Hom}_R(Ra_!K,R)
$$

induces on $H^i$ the adjunction bijection
$\operatorname{Hom}(K,\omega_{X,R}[i])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Ra_!K,R[i])$ of
$Ra_!\dashv Ra^!_R$, so it is an isomorphism. As a consequence, it agrees with
the limit of the finite adjunctions. The finite exceptional adjoints of
[thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] and the compact-support reduction
[lem-coef-integral-compact-support] give, by derived extension and restriction of
scalars,

$$
\begin{aligned}
R\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,\omega_{X,R})
&\cong R\varprojlim_n R\operatorname{Hom}_{X,A_n}(K_n,\omega_{X,n})\\
&\cong R\varprojlim_n R\operatorname{Hom}_{A_n}(Ra_{!,n}K_n,A_n)
\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_R(Ra_!K,R).
\end{aligned}
$$

Here the middle isomorphism is the finite adjunction on derived mapping
complexes: it is [prop-asd-internal-adjunction] on the étale site, transported by
the finite site comparisons. The counits are compatible with reduction
([sk-prop-scalar-six]), so the two descriptions agree.
